title: Char Siu Pork
subtitle: Cantonese barbecued pork with a sweet-sticky glaze
excerpt: The iconic Cantonese roast: strips of pork shoulder marinated in a deeply savoury-sweet mixture of hoisin, honey, five spice, and soy sauce, then roasted until caramelised and sticky with a characteristic brick-red colour.

recipe.sourceNotes: Char siu (叉燒) means fork-roasted in Cantonese, referring to the traditional preparation of skewering the pork on long forks and roasting it over charcoal. It is one of the most important preparations in Cantonese cuisine and a staple of Cantonese barbecue restaurants (siu mei shops) where it hangs alongside roasted ducks and whole pigs. The brick-red colour comes traditionally from red fermented tofu (nam yu) or red food colouring; home versions achieve a similar look and flavour through the deep caramelisation of honey and hoisin without the colouring. Char siu is eaten as a stand-alone dish with rice or noodles, used as a filling in char siu bao (barbecued pork buns), added to fried rice, or sliced and served as part of a roasted meat platter.

recipeTools.notes: A roasting tin with a rack.

content.text: Marinate for at least 4 hours, overnight is better. Use pork shoulder or pork neck for the best result: both have enough fat and connective tissue to stay moist during the high-heat roasting. Glaze during the last 10 minutes of cooking and again after resting for maximum stickiness. Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

items.preparation: cut into long strips about 4 cm wide and 3 cm thick

content.text: Mix all the marinade ingredients together. Coat the pork strips thoroughly, cover, and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or overnight. Remove from the fridge 30 minutes before cooking.

Heat the oven to 220 C (200 C fan). Place a rack over a roasting tin filled with 1 cm of water (this prevents drips burning). Lay the pork strips on the rack and roast for 25 minutes, turning halfway. Brush with the reserved marinade and a little extra honey and roast for a further 10 minutes until the pork is caramelised and slightly charred at the edges.
Rest for 10 minutes. Brush once more with honey while still hot. Slice thickly and serve with steamed rice, sliced cucumber, and spring onion.
